To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) MA packaging of fresh produce is an effective means of extending its postharvest life, and 2) a suitable film for each fresh commodity must be chosen based on its permeability, respiration rate, and other factors such as temperature and relative humidity.
the MA of fruits and vegetables can be used to extend the shelf-life of these commodities, and that MA is most effective when applied immediately post-harvest and in combination with refrigeration.

(1) the MA of fruits and vegetables can be controlled by the selection of the appropriate packaging film, (2) the MA of the commodity is a function of the permeability of film and the respiration rate of the commodity, (3) the MA can be modified by controlling the permeability of packaging films, and (4) the MA of commodities can be controlled by selecting the appropriate packaging film.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of mathematical models that can be used to design MA packaging systems for fresh produce.

1) developing mathematical models to predict MA in commodity/film/packaging systems, 2) evaluating the effect of various film properties on MA development, 3) developing methods for evaluating the suitability of a given film for a particular commodity, and 4) developing MA packaging systems for specific commodities.
developing a better understanding of the mechanisms of deterioration of fresh fruits and the effects of MA on the quality of fresh produce.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MA is a useful supplement to temperature and RH control in maintaining the quality and extending the postharvest life of fresh fruits and vegetable.
MA is an effective tool in extending the shelf life of fresh produce.
the use of modified atmospheres for the preservation of quality of fresh fruits, vegetables, and flowers is an effective technology, provided that the MA is maintained at optimum levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MA packaging of fruits and/or vegetables is a useful technique to maintain the quality of fresh produce during storage and distribution.
the most suitable film should be selected for the commodity, and that the film should be sealed to a package of the appropriate size to ensure that a suitable MA will be attained within the package.
the use of a MA in packaging fresh produce can be beneficial in extending the storage life of many commodities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a single film for a given commodity may not provide optimum conditions for all the commodities that are packed together.
the MA of fresh produce is a dynamic equilibrium that is affected by the commodity, packaging system, and environment.
the use of MA in combination with refrigeration is an effective means of extending the shelf life and maintaining the quality of fruits and vegetables during storage and distribution.
